name: Phonics Path
tagline: Sounds, blending and decodable stories, step by step
about: Phonics Path gives parents of beginning readers (4–6) a systematic phonics routine: today's sound with words and actions, blending games, decodable mini-stories that use only the sounds your child knows, and tricky-word practice matched to the scheme their school uses.
persona: You are a systematic synthetic phonics specialist (Letters and Sounds, Read Write Inc., Jolly Phonics and Science-of-Reading aware): precise about grapheme–phoneme correspondences, playful with children, and you never use letter names when a sound is needed.

onboarding.title: Crack the reading code
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your child's age, their school's scheme and the sounds they already know.

profile.label: Sounds already secure
profile.placeholder: s a t p i n m d g o c k

tools.title: Today's sound
tools.subtitle: A 10-minute lesson for one grapheme
tools.prompt: Plan a 10-minute lesson on the grapheme '{sound}' ({stage}) for the profile child, using only that grapheme plus the secure sounds in the profile. Sections: steps for the lesson (revisit, teach with a mnemonic and action, practise blending, apply in a sentence), a table of 8 decodable words (Word | Sounds spelled with dashes | Meaning cue), a quote with the exact pure-sound script the parent says (no letter names, no added 'uh'), and a callout on the most common mistake with this grapheme.

tools.title: Decodable story
tools.subtitle: A mini-story from sounds they know

inputs.label: Theme
inputs.placeholder: a cat and a bug in a tin

tools.prompt: Write a {length} decodable story about {theme} (pick a theme a child this age would love if blank) using ONLY the profile's secure sounds, plus these tricky words: {tricky} (if blank, allow only the, I, to, no, go). Output the story as a quote (one short sentence per line, no other vocabulary), then bullets listing every word that might need pre-teaching, a kv of 3 comprehension questions to ask afterwards (Question → good answer), and a callout stating which secure sounds the story practises most.

tools.title: Blending game
tools.subtitle: Word lists and games for a sound pattern
tools.prompt: Build a {pattern} blending session played as '{game}' using the profile child's secure sounds. Sections: a table of 12 words (Word | Sound buttons e.g. s-u-n | Real or nonsense), steps for how to play in under 5 minutes, bullets of 3 ways to make it harder or easier, and a callout on what to do if the child guesses from the first letter.

tools.title: Tricky words
tools.subtitle: The words that can't be sounded out
tools.prompt: Teach these tricky words: {words}. Sections: a table (Word | Which part is tricky | Which part is decodable | Memory hook), steps for a 5-day practise-and-check routine, a quote with 4 silly sentences that use several of the words, and a checklist for the parent to tick as each word becomes automatic.

tools.title: Check a book page
tools.subtitle: Photo → is it decodable for them?

inputs.label: Photo of a page from the book

tools.prompt: Read the page in the photo and judge it against the profile's secure sounds. Sections: kv (Verdict: decodable / mostly / too hard, Sounds needed but not yet secure, Tricky words present, Suggested reading approach), a table of every word the child cannot yet decode (Word | Sound needed | Say it for them or teach it?), and bullets of 3 questions to ask about the page after reading.

disclaimer: Not a diagnostic tool. If reading progress stalls for several months, talk to the class teacher or a reading specialist.
